name: GET /api/users/register - The team register with its lifecycle states
description: Returns every account with its derived state - pending, active or deactivated - together with who invited it, when it was opened and when it was closed. Proves criterion 4c12f924-87d1-4be1-b790-d94a936d58b3#AC4 from the read side: a deactivated colleague is still ON the register, with deactivated_at and deactivated_by recorded, which is what makes their past actions attributable rather than orphaned. Pass deactivated=true to include closed accounts; the default hides them because the list exists to be worked and archive rows would bury the pending invitations that are outstanding tasks. SEPARATE from GET /api/users, which every screen that must name a colleague already calls: widening that response with invitation stamps would push administrative data into the routing, coverage and ownership screens, and narrowing it later would break them. Three states rather than a boolean, because an invitation nobody has opened and an account closed after somebody left are the same is_active=false and completely different facts. local_credentials_permitted is stated by the API rather than guessed by the client, since whether an administrator may issue a password here is a deployment fact. QA: depends on register and login for the bearer token, and on invite so the register is non-empty.

testCases.name: The working register, pending invitations first
Closed accounts are still on the register when asked for
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all

errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, or present without a bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
